**Discussion-Based Assessments (DBAs) at Texas Tech K-12**

- **Purpose:** Discussion-Based Assessments (DBAs) are used to verify student understanding, ensure academic integrity, and provide an opportunity for students to demonstrate mastery of course material in a live, interactive format.
- **Format:** DBAs typically involve a live, camera-enabled session between the student and the teacher. During the assessment, students may be asked to explain concepts, answer questions, or discuss topics covered in the course.
- **When Required:** DBAs may be required at certain checkpoints in a course, before a final exam, or when a teacher needs to verify the authenticity of submitted work.
- **Scheduling:** Students will be notified by their teacher when a DBA is required and will receive instructions on how to schedule and participate in the session.
- **Expectations:** Students should be prepared to discuss their coursework, demonstrate their understanding, and answer questions independently. Appropriate attire and a distraction-free environment are expected during video-based activities.

**Important Notes:**
- If a teacher cannot reasonably verify the authenticity of submitted work, a DBA or similar verification method may be required.
- Work determined to be inauthentic may be subject to resubmission requirements and academic consequences according to Texas Tech K-12 policy.

**Next Steps:**
- If you have been asked to complete a DBA, follow your teacher’s instructions for scheduling and preparation.
- For questions about DBAs or if you need assistance, contact your teacher through the course communication tools or reach out to Texas Tech K-12 support at 1-800-692-6877 or ttuk12@ttu.edu.

AI (artificial intelligence) use policy

Artificial intelligence (AI) tools may be used to support student learning when their use is appropriate for the assignment or activity. AI should support, not replace, a student's own learning, critical thinking and communication.

Appropriate uses of AI may include brainstorming, clarifying concepts, creating study materials, generating practice questions or receiving feedback when permitted by the teacher or course.

**Accommodations and Supports for Students with ADHD, Dyslexia, or Other Learning Differences at Texas Tech K-12**

**General Approach**
- Texas Tech K-12 is committed to providing accessible education and meeting the needs of students with disabilities, including ADHD, dyslexia, and other learning differences.
- The program is fully online and asynchronous, so all services and accommodations are provided virtually.

**Eligibility and Documentation**
- To qualify for accommodations, students must provide appropriate documentation:
  - A current Section 504 Plan, or
  - The most recent Admission, Review, and Dismissal (ARD)/Individualized Education Program (IEP), along with the most recent evaluation report.

**Accommodation Request Process**
- **Full-Time Students:** Submit documentation at the time of enrollment. Documentation is reviewed by appropriate personnel, and a committee meeting may be convened to determine supports and services.
- **Part-Time/Supplemental Students:** Submit accommodation requests through the Focus portal under "Forms." Documentation will be reviewed, and approved accommodations will be implemented accordingly.
  - [Focus Portal](https://ttu.focusschoolsoftware.com/focus/)

**Types of Accommodations**
- Common accommodations for students with ADHD, dyslexia, or other learning differences may include:
  - Extended time on exams and assignments
  - Use of screen readers or text-to-speech tools
  - Larger font or color change functionality
  - Distraction-free testing environments
  - Flexible scheduling
  - Access to teacher office hours for additional support
  - Other supports as specified in the student’s IEP or 504 Plan

**Important Notes**
- Accommodations applied to one course do not automatically apply to others; specify which courses need accommodations.
- The ARD or 504 committee must determine if the fully online, asynchronous program is the appropriate setting and least restrictive environment for the student.
- Texas Tech K-12’s online courses are fully accessible and meet Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.0.

**Support Contacts**
- For more information or to request accommodations, contact:
  - Lesley Stone: [Create Case](https://www.support.k12.ttu.edu/k12?id=report_issue&sys_id=043a96811b358e50239f0e1de54bcbeb)
  - Terri Raney: [Create Case](https://www.support.k12.ttu.edu/k12?id=report_issue&sys_id=043a96811b358e50239f0e1de54bcbeb)
  - General support: 1-800-692-6877 or ttuk12@ttu.edu

**Is Texas Tech K-12 a Good Fit?**
- Many students with learning differences do well in the program, especially those needing accommodations like screen readers, larger text, or extended time.
- The program may not be suitable for students who require in-person services that cannot be provided virtually.

**Next Step**
- If you are considering enrollment, gather your documentation and submit an accommodation request as early as possible to ensure timely support. If you have questions about whether the program is a good fit, contact the support team for more information.

How do I create a Parent Portal account?

Parents please click here to create your Parent Portal Account (opens in new tab)

Link for "Parents please click here to create your Parent Portal Account (opens in new tab)": https://ttu.focusschoolsoftware.com/focus/auth/

Parents, if you have not created your account, please visit our Parent Portal Registration (opens in new tab) page. The Parent portal will allow you to monitor your child's progress in school by providing timely access to both assignments and grades that are entered by the teacher throughout the grading period. You will also have the ability to contact your student's teacher via the "Communications" module inside of Focus.

Link for "Parent Portal Registration (opens in new tab)": https://ttu.focusschoolsoftware.com/focus/auth

In order to create a Parent Portal account online, you must have a valid email address. Please note that the email should not be the same as the student's email.

Texas Tech K-12 requires every user to have a unique email address to ensure any communication goes to the intended recipient. Parents and Students cannot share email addresses. The Password Reset Email will not work if more than one user shares an email address. Most ISP or email providers have options for families who need multiple email addresses on the same account for each user.

Prior to starting the account creation process, we ask that if your student has an existing account, you please have their matriculation number and date of birth. The system will request this information to connect the accounts.

For those that do not have an existing account, please click on "I do not have an Account Registered on the Parent Portal but would like to Create One" (opens in new tab).

Link for "I do not have an Account Registered on the Parent Portal but would like to Create One" (opens in new tab)": https://ttu.focusschoolsoftware.com/focus/auth/

Attendance/Progress Requirements

Step 1: In your all-online program, attendance “will” be defined as progress within each semester course.

Step 2: You will have six months to complete each semester course.

Step 3: You must maintain enrollment in a minimum of four semester courses.

Step 4: You must make weekly progress in each course by working in each course a minimum of three days per 7-day period.

Step 5: You must complete a minimum of 5% of course assignments in every seven-day period. For example, if your course has 20 assignments, you need to complete a minimum of one per week. If your course has 60 assignments, you must average a minimum of three per week.

Please note:

Step 1: Completing the minimum number of assignments does not guaranteed you will complete within the 6-month time frame.

Step 2: Completing the minimum number of assignments and courses may not maintain your appropriate grade level or anticipated graduation date.

Step 3: If your progress is adequate, your parent may request “vacation” days.

Step 4: Extensions are not available, so you must schedule your weekly progress to complete the minimum of four courses during the 6-month period.

Step 5: Failure to meet minimum progress requirements may cause Texas Tech K-12 to implement truancy processes and may result in your removal from the program.

Is this school a good fit for a student with special needs?

This is the parent’s decision.  Of course, you know your child best and you are the best person to determine the environment in which your child will experience the most success.

Many students with special needs do very well in our online program. Some of these needs that are readily accommodated include:  use of a screen reader, need larger font, need highlighting or color change functionality, need a learning environment free from distractions, need extended time on exams, have social anxiety, have medical concerns. Our online courses are fully accessible and meet Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.0 federal web compliance requirements.

Texas Tech K-12 may not be the most appropriate instructional setting and the least restrictive environment for your child (see above), as required by federal law.

Texas Tech K-12 is a statewide online school district and does not have a physical campus nor a geographic service district. We serve full-time students from across the entire state of Texas.

We have special education personnel to ensure and monitor appropriate accommodations identified in the Individualized Education Program or 504 plan. We closely monitor the academic progress of all students and will provide appropriate interventions and services as identified.

Again, as the parent, you will need to make an individualized analysis. We are happy to share more information about the nature of our coursework if that would be helpful in your decision-making process.

Minimum Lesson/Unit Completion Requirements

Students demonstrate attendance in Texas Tech K-12 online school by regularly completing assignments. Attendance is directly tied to what the student accomplishes and/or produces over a given period. The assignments completed are evidence that a student has been in attendance. If no work is produced, the student is not considered to be in attendance.

Unless specifically stated otherwise, attendance is required a minimum of three days per week. A student must complete at least 5% of course assignments in a seven-day period and in every subsequent seven-day period until the course is completed.

Course completion is required to earn course credit. No partial course credit will be granted. Course credit is earned when the student has successfully demonstrated mastery of the Texas Essential Knowledge and Skills for the course.

Students have six months from the date of enrollment to complete each course. To remain in the program, students must be concurrently enrolled in a minimum of four courses.

Failure to meet minimum progress or attendance requirements may result in attendance interventions and an administrative review of the student's enrollment status.

Participation in mandatory state testing is a condition of enrollment in our tuition free program and is a requirement from the Texas Education Agency for graduation under the Foundation High School program. Students who do not participate in state testing will be moved to the tuition paid program.

**Parental Supervision Requirements at Texas Tech K-12**

**Full-Time Tuition-Free Program (TX Residents Only)**
- **Learning Coach Role:** Each student is required to have a designated Learning Coach—usually a parent, guardian, or another responsible adult.
- **Responsibilities of the Learning Coach:**
  - Monitor student progress and lesson mastery.
  - Review student work and communicate with teachers as needed.
  - Help establish a daily routine and ensure the student is meeting attendance and progress requirements (minimum of three days per week and at least 5% of course assignments completed each week).
- **Daily Supervision:** The amount of daily supervision needed depends on the student’s age, grade level, and ability to work independently:
  - **Elementary Students:** Typically require more hands-on daily supervision and support with lessons, assignments, and time management.
  - **Middle/High School Students:** May require less direct supervision but still benefit from daily check-ins to ensure they are staying on track, especially if they are new to online learning or need organizational support.

**Tuition-Paid and Supplemental Programs**
- Parental involvement is still important, especially for younger students, but the level of supervision can be adjusted based on the student’s independence and academic needs.

**Key Points**
- Parents/guardians are expected to be actively involved, especially for younger students.
- The Learning Coach is a critical support role for student success in the online, self-paced environment.
- Older or more independent students may require less daily supervision but should still have regular parental oversight.

**Resources**
- [Learning Coach Information (PDF)](https://www.depts.ttu.edu/k12/freetuition/learning-coach/)

**Next Step**
- Consider your student’s age, learning style, and independence when planning for daily supervision. If you have questions about the Learning Coach role or expectations, contact Texas Tech K-12 at 1-800-692-6877 or ttuk12@ttu.edu.

**Implementation of Existing 504 Accommodations at Texas Tech K-12**

- **Yes, Texas Tech K-12 can implement existing Section 504 accommodations** for eligible students, provided the accommodations are appropriate for the fully online, asynchronous instructional setting.

**Process for Implementing 504 Accommodations:**
- **Submit Documentation:** Provide a copy of the current Section 504 Plan during enrollment (for full-time students) or through the Focus portal under "Forms" (for part-time/supplemental students).
- **Review and Planning:** Documentation will be reviewed by appropriate personnel. A committee meeting may be convened, if needed, to determine how best to implement the accommodations in the online environment.
- **Implementation:** Approved accommodations will be put in place in accordance with state and federal requirements, ensuring access to the curriculum while maintaining program integrity.

**Important Notes:**
- Some accommodations may need to be adapted for the online format. The ARD or 504 committee will determine if the Texas Tech K-12 program is the appropriate setting and least restrictive environment for your child.
- Accommodations applied to one course do not automatically apply to others; please specify which courses need accommodations.

**Next Steps:**
- Submit your student’s current Section 504 Plan and any supporting documentation as soon as possible.
- For questions or to begin the process, contact Texas Tech K-12 at 1-800-692-6877, ttuk12@ttu.edu, or submit a request through the [Support Portal](https://www.support.k12.ttu.edu/k12?id=report_issue&sys_id=043a96811b358e50239f0e1de54bcbeb).

- **IEP Implementation:** Texas Tech K-12 can implement an existing Individualized Education Program (IEP) and provide special education services that are appropriate for a fully online, asynchronous instructional setting.
- **Eligibility and Admission:** To qualify, the student’s IEP must indicate that Texas Tech K-12’s online program is the appropriate instructional setting and the student’s least restrictive environment. The Admission, Review, and Dismissal (ARD) committee is responsible for determining if the online program meets the student’s needs.
- **Process:**
  - Submit the most recent IEP and evaluation report during enrollment.
  - Documentation is reviewed by special education personnel.
  - A committee meeting may be convened to determine appropriate supports and services in alignment with the online environment.
  - Approved accommodations and services will be implemented in accordance with state and federal requirements.
- **Service Limitations:** Texas Tech K-12 provides only services that can be delivered virtually, as the school does not have a physical location. In-person or hands-on services that require a physical presence cannot be provided.
- **Ongoing Support:** Special education personnel monitor the implementation of IEP accommodations and the student’s academic progress, providing interventions and services as identified in the IEP.

**Important Notes:**
- The ARD committee must determine that the online, asynchronous program is the most appropriate and least restrictive environment for the student.
- Some services or supports may need to be adapted for the virtual setting.

**Next Step:**
- If you are considering enrollment and your student may qualify for special education services, contact Texas Tech K-12 at 1-800-692-6877 or ttuk12@ttu.edu to discuss your student’s needs and begin the documentation review process.
